subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should ordinary Discord and bound ACP-thread messages bypass busy reply-operation or channel admission to reach active-run queue policy by default, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 be the canonical repair path?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes message ordering, fallback behavior, and session-state admission across channels, so maintainer intent is needed before automation creates a duplicate or conflicting repair.

options.title: Refresh the admission PR
options.body: Rebase or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 and require proof that no-visible fallback, terminal-session recovery, and ordinary same-session steering all behave correctly.

options.title: Limit steering to explicit controls
options.body: Keep ordinary messages serialized for now, document command-only steering as the supported path, and close or narrow the remaining ordinary-message request.

options.title: Split Discord ACP from broader steering
options.body: Track a smaller Discord/ACP admission fix separately while leaving https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 as the broader cross-channel steering umbrella.

recommendation.title: Refresh the admission PR
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 and require proof that no-visible fallback, terminal-session recovery, and ordinary same-session steering all behave correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the recent partial steering fix and are the strongest current-main provenance signal for deciding whether the remaining admission change should follow that direction.
